title: APSU students protest in Clarksville following discovery of a noose on campus

tea.why: Students protested the discovery of a noose on campus and expressed dissatisfaction with the university's communication and handling of the event.
tea.want: Students demanded increased campus security, more cameras, transparency regarding the investigation, and clearer guidelines on racial injustice.
tea.changed: Nov 25: The Montgomery County District Attorney's Office announced that no criminal charges will be filed regarding the incident.

summary: On November 23, 2026, students at Austin Peay State University (APSU) in Clarksville, Tennessee, held a protest following the discovery of a noose near a campus residence hall on November 20. Organized by student groups including Men of Excellence, the Black Student Alliance, and People of Praise, in collaboration with Black Clarksville, the demonstration involved hundreds of students marching through campus. Participants demanded greater transparency, accountability, and improved security measures. Following the march, university leadership held a community conversation where President Mike Licari acknowledged mishandling the situation. While the university initially stated the act was not motivated by racial hatred, students expressed continued frustration. On November 25, the Montgomery County District Attorney's Office stated that after reviewing state law, it determined the incident did not constitute a criminal violation.
demands: Installation of more cameras near residence halls
Clearer guidelines for handling racial injustice
response: APSU President Mike Licari admitted to mishandling the situation during a community session. The university stated it is limited by federal law in what it can disclose about the student involved, who came forward to campus police. The Montgomery County DA found no criminal violation.

crowd.text: Sources reported the protest numbered well over 50 students, while another source described the crowd as hundreds.

updates.text: APSU police responded to a report of a noose hanging from a tree near a residence hall.
Students held a protest march on campus to demand transparency and accountability regarding the incident.
The Montgomery County District Attorney's Office announced that no criminal charges will be filed.
